en.headline: Development Bureau says Hung Hom twin towers will not block Lion Rock view
en.dek: Permanent Secretary Doris Ho said the revised waterfront plan includes a public viewing platform and about 200 yacht berths while increasing residential floor area.
body: The Development Bureau's Permanent Secretary Doris Ho said on Wednesday that plans for twin towers on the Hung Hom waterfront will not block the view of Lion Rock or affect the ridgeline.

The revised proposal features two connected buildings with an elevated viewing platform overlooking Victoria Harbour. Ho said the platform will be open to the public, with any entry fee to be decided based on the project's financial viability.

The total floor area remains similar to an earlier proposal, but commercial space has been reduced and residential floor area increased after market feedback. About five per cent of the floor area is allocated to a yacht club providing around 200 berths, the maximum without affecting navigation channels.

Ho said the development aims to inject vitality into the older Hung Hom area and create a landmark. The project is divided into waterfront and inland zones, and the government is studying whether to release the site in one parcel or two. The target to hand over the first batch of land by 2029 remains unchanged.

zh.headline: 發展局指紅磡雙塔發展不會阻擋獅子山景觀
zh.dek: 發展局常任秘書長何珮玲表示，修訂後的海濱計劃包括公眾觀景台及約200個遊艇泊位，並增加住宅樓面。
body: 發展局常任秘書長何珮玲周三表示，紅磡海濱雙塔發展計劃不會阻擋獅子山景觀，亦不會影響山脊線。
修訂方案包括兩座相連建築及高架觀景台，可俯瞰維港。何珮玲指觀景台會開放予公眾，是否收費則視乎項目財務可行性。
總樓面面積與早前方案相若，但因應市場意見減少商業樓面、增加住宅樓面。約百分之五樓面用作遊艇會，提供約200個泊位，為不影響航道的上限。
何珮玲稱發展旨在為較舊的紅磡區注入活力，並成為地標。項目分海濱及內陸兩區，政府正研究以單一幅或兩幅土地推出。2029年首批土地移交目標維持不變。
